root_cause.text: act_ct was allowed to bind to egress qdiscs (non-ingress/clsact) that do not properly handle the TC_ACT_CONSUMED return code, causing a use-after-free when the connection tracking defragmentation engine later accesses a skb that has already been freed.
root_cause.evidence: CVE description states "classify can return TC_ACT_CONSUMED while the current skb being held by the defragmentation engine... may cause a UaF when the defrag engine later on tries to tuch again such packet." The patch adds a check in `tcf_ct_init` to reject binding unless the action is attached to an ingress or clsact qdisc (or a shared block), and defines `TCA_ACT_FLAGS_AT_INGRESS_OR_CLSACT` flag set only for those qdiscs. The commit message explicitly cites the blamed commit (`3f14b377d01d`) and notes that only clsact/ingress qdiscs handle TC_ACT_CONSUMED correctly.
